notes.meaning: The Lord spoke to Moses with direct instructions for setting up the tabernacle. Moses did not rush ahead on his own schedule; he waited until God gave the word.

God told Moses to erect the tent on New Year's Day, exactly one year after the first Passover season began in Egypt. The people had spent about six months preparing and crafting every part. Starting the new year with God's dwelling showed that worshiping him was their top priority.

Moses was instructed to place the ark inside the Most Holy Place first of all. This wooden chest held the two stone tablets of the Ten Commandments, which served as a witness to God's covenant with Israel. The inner curtain was then hung to shield this sacred room from view.

Moses was told to bring in the table and arrange the twelve loaves of bread on it. He was also to set up the gold lampstand and light its seven lamps. Both pieces stood in the outer room, called the Holy Place.

The gold altar for burning sweet incense was placed in front of the inner curtain, directly facing the ark. Moses was also told to hang the curtain at the tent entrance. This screen closed off the Holy Place from the courtyard outside.

The bronze altar for burnt offerings was positioned outside in the courtyard, right before the doorway of the tent. Animal sacrifices were offered here so that smoke and ashes stayed out in the open air.
The bronze basin was placed between the tent entrance and the bronze altar and filled with water. The priests needed this water to wash their hands and feet before performing any sacred service.

Moses was told to set up the curtains that enclosed the large courtyard around the tabernacle. He also hung the colourful screen at the courtyard gate. This separated the holy grounds from the rest of Israel's camp.

God commanded Moses to pour the sacred anointing oil over the tabernacle, its furnishings, the bronze altar, and the washbasin. Anointing set these items apart exclusively for God's holy use. The bronze altar became especially holy, making anything that touched it holy as well.

Moses was directed to bring Aaron and his sons to the courtyard entrance and wash them thoroughly with water. Aaron was then dressed in his special high-priestly robes and anointed with oil. Washing showed their need to be cleansed from sin before serving in God's presence.

Aaron's sons were brought forward, dressed in linen tunics, and anointed to serve as priests under their father. This single ordination established their family line as priests for all future generations of Israel.
Moses obeyed every instruction just as the Lord had commanded him. He showed total faithfulness by following God's exact pattern rather than adding his own ideas.
The tabernacle was finally raised on the first day of the first month in the second year after the exodus. Raising God's tent on New Year's Day gave the entire nation a holy beginning.

Moses set the heavy silver bases in place and fitted the upright wooden frames into them. He locked the walls together with crossbars, set up the pillars, and spread the tent cloth and tough outer leather coverings over the roof.

Moses placed the two stone tablets of the law inside the ark and attached the carrying poles. He placed the gold mercy seat on top and brought the ark into the Most Holy Place, hanging the thick veil to conceal it from view.
Moses placed the table on the north side of the Holy Place, outside the inner veil. He set out twelve fresh loaves of bread in two rows before the Lord, just as God had commanded.
Moses set up the gold lampstand on the south side of the Holy Place, directly across from the table. He lit the lamps before the Lord so that light filled the holy room.
Moses placed the gold altar inside the Holy Place right in front of the veil. He burned fragrant incense upon it, letting the sweet smoke rise up before the Lord.
Moses hung the entrance curtain at the doorway of the tent. In the courtyard outside, he set up the bronze altar and presented the very first burnt offering and grain offering upon it.

Moses positioned the bronze basin between the tent and the altar and filled it with water. Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet there whenever they approached the altar or entered the tent. Regular washing reminded them that God requires clean hands and pure hearts in his service.
Moses set up the curtains around the courtyard and hung the screen at the main entrance gate. With that final step, the great work of building God's sanctuary was completed.

As soon as the work was finished, the cloud covered the tent and the bright glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. God showed that he accepted their work and had come to live in the middle of his people.

The radiant brightness of God's presence was so overwhelming that even Moses could not step inside the tent. This showed the awesome majesty of God and human weakness in the presence of his pure glory.

From that time on, the movement of the cloud guided Israel on their journeys. Whenever the cloud rose from the tabernacle, the people packed up and followed it; but if the cloud stayed, they remained in camp.

The cloud of the Lord remained over the tabernacle by day, and fire glowed within it by night in full view of all Israel. God never left them, faithfully guiding his people through all forty years in the wilderness.
